title: The Use of Model Output Statistics (MOS) in Objective Weather Forecasting
relevance_note: Origin of MOS: regress observations on NWP output at station locations; defines the paradigm the whole field extends.

title: Calibrated Probabilistic Forecasting Using Ensemble Model Output Statistics and Minimum CRPS Estimation
relevance_note: EMOS / nonhomogeneous Gaussian regression. THE reference method for 2m temperature; single Gaussian with mean affine in members and variance affine in ensemble variance, fitted by minimum CRPS.

title: Using Bayesian Model Averaging to Calibrate Forecast Ensembles
relevance_note: BMA: predictive distribution as weighted mixture of member-conditioned kernels. Main alternative to EMOS; heavier to fit, rarely better for T2m.

title: Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
relevance_note: Theory of proper scoring rules; why CRPS is the right training and verification target.

title: Probabilistic Forecasts, Calibration and Sharpness
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B (Statistical Methodology)
relevance_note: Sharpness-subject-to-calibration paradigm; the evaluation philosophy behind all postprocessing benchmarks.

title: Calibrated Surface Temperature Forecasts from the Canadian Ensemble Prediction System Using Bayesian Model Averaging
relevance_note: Early operational BMA for surface temperature over a large station network (Canada).

title: Probabilistic Forecast Calibration Using ECMWF and GFS Ensemble Reforecasts. Part I: Two-Meter Temperatures
relevance_note: Reforecast-calibrated 2m temperature; quantifies how much of ensemble error is systematic and correctable, and how training length matters.

title: Probabilistic Forecast Calibration Using ECMWF and GFS Ensemble Reforecasts. Part II: Precipitation
relevance_note: Companion precipitation study; contrast case for why temperature is the easy first variable.

title: Calibrating Multimodel Forecast Ensembles with Exchangeable and Missing Members Using Bayesian Model Averaging
relevance_note: Handling exchangeable and MISSING ensemble members - directly relevant to gappy station/member archives.

title: A review on statistical postprocessing methods for hydrometeorological ensemble forecasting
relevance_note: Hydrometeorological postprocessing review; complementary taxonomy, more on precipitation and multivariate structure.

title: Univariate Ensemble Postprocessing
relevance_note: Wilks' textbook chapter on univariate ensemble postprocessing - the cleanest formal treatment of EMOS/BMA/logistic regression.

title: Statistical Postprocessing for Weather Forecasts: Review, Challenges, and Avenues in a Big Data World
venue: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
relevance_note: The field review. Read first: taxonomy of methods, verification practice, and open problems.

title: Gridded, locally calibrated, probabilistic temperature forecasts based on ensemble model output statistics
venue: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society
relevance_note: Gridded, locally calibrated probabilistic temperature via EMOS - the station-to-grid extrapolation problem.

theme: 3. Extending classical models (boosting, standardized anomalies, time/space structure)
title: Spatial postprocessing of ensemble forecasts for temperature using nonhomogeneous Gaussian regression
relevance_note: Spatial extension of NGR for temperature with locally adaptive climatology; Gaussian random field vs ECC for spatial dependence.

theme: 3. Extending classical models (boosting, standardized anomalies, time/space structure)
title: Nonhomogeneous Boosting for Predictor Selection in Ensemble Postprocessing
relevance_note: Boosting for predictor selection inside nonhomogeneous regression: how to add many predictors to EMOS without overfitting. The strongest classical benchmark in Rasp and Lerch.

theme: 3. Extending classical models (boosting, standardized anomalies, time/space structure)
title: Spatial ensemble post‐processing with standardized anomalies
venue: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society
relevance_note: SAMOS: standardized anomalies let ONE model be fitted across many stations at once, removing site and seasonal effects. Key precursor to pooled training.

theme: 3. Extending classical models (boosting, standardized anomalies, time/space structure)
title: Estimation Methods for Nonhomogeneous Regression Models: Minimum Continuous Ranked Probability Score versus Maximum Likelihood
relevance_note: Estimation choices for nonhomogeneous regression: minimum CRPS vs maximum likelihood. Matters for small per-station samples.

theme: 3. Extending classical models (boosting, standardized anomalies, time/space structure)
title: Probabilistic Temperature Forecasting with a Heteroscedastic Autoregressive Ensemble Postprocessing model
venue: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society
relevance_note: Heteroscedastic autoregressive EMOS for temperature: explicit treatment of error autocorrelation in time.

theme: 3. Extending classical models (boosting, standardized anomalies, time/space structure)
title: Remember the past: a comparison of time-adaptive training schemes for non-homogeneous regression
relevance_note: Time-adaptive training schemes for NGR on central-European 2m temperature; how to handle seasonality without a long archive.

theme: 3. Extending classical models (boosting, standardized anomalies, time/space structure)
title: Time‐series‐based ensemble model output statistics for temperature forecasts postprocessing
venue: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society
relevance_note: Time-series EMOS for temperature with seasonality, trend and autoregressive error structure.

title: Statistical postprocessing of ensemble forecasts for severe weather at Deutscher Wetterdienst
relevance_note: DWD's operational Ensemble-MOS: what a national service actually runs, and how they treat extremes.

title: From research to applications – examples of operational ensemble post-processing in France using machine learning
relevance_note: Meteo-France operational ML postprocessing at industrial scale, incl. station-based temperature then interpolation to grid.

title: Operational statistical postprocessing of temperature ensemble forecasts with station‐specific predictors
relevance_note: Operational station-specific EMOS-type calibration of ECMWF ENS temperature to 240 h over Europe (FMI). Closest operational analogue to the user's setup.

title: IMPROVER: The New Probabilistic Postprocessing System at the Met Office
venue: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
relevance_note: IMPROVER, the Met Office probabilistic postprocessing system - the framework used in the AIFS postprocessing test below.

title: Calibrated Ensemble Forecasts Using Quantile Regression Forests and Ensemble Model Output Statistics
relevance_note: QRF postprocessing: nonparametric, arbitrary predictors, no distributional assumption. Beat EMOS on Meteo-France PEARP temperature and wind.

title: Neural networks for post-processing ensemble weather forecasts
relevance_note: THE anchor. Distributional regression network for 2m temperature at German stations; introduces STATION EMBEDDINGS in a single globally-pooled network.

title: Ensemble Postprocessing Using Quantile Function Regression Based on Neural Networks and Bernstein Polynomials
relevance_note: Bernstein quantile network: neural net outputs a flexible quantile function rather than Gaussian parameters. Standard BQN benchmark.

title: Forest-Based and Semiparametric Methods for the Postprocessing of Rainfall Ensemble Forecasting
relevance_note: Forest-based and semiparametric postprocessing (rainfall); shows how tree methods handle the non-Gaussian case.

title: Machine learning methods for postprocessing ensemble forecasts of wind gusts: A systematic comparison
relevance_note: The honest benchmark: 8 methods (EMOS, MBM, IDR, gradient-boosted EMOS, QRF, DRN, BQN, HEN) on 175 German stations, 6 years. Best single source for realistic skill ordering.

title: Deep learning for post-processing ensemble weather forecasts
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Sciences
relevance_note: Deep learning postprocessing on gridded fields; encoder-decoder view rather than station view.

title: A transformer neural network for predicting <scp>near‐surface</scp> temperature
relevance_note: Transformer postprocessing of 2m temperature trained on >1000 private weather stations; reports bias/STD for raw NWP, LR, NN and transformer. Coastal dependence noted.

title: Postprocessing of Ensemble Weather Forecasts Using Permutation-invariant Neural Networks
venue: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
relevance_note: Permutation-invariant networks treat the ensemble as an unordered SET rather than summary statistics; finds most information sits in few ensemble degrees of freedom.

title: Physics-Constrained Deep Learning Postprocessing of Temperature and Humidity
venue: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
relevance_note: Physics-constrained deep-learning postprocessing enforcing thermodynamic consistency between temperature and humidity; advantage largest when DATA ARE SCARCE.

title: Self-Attentive Transformer for Fast and Accurate Postprocessing of Temperature and Wind Speed Forecasts
venue: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
relevance_note: Transformer postprocessing all lead times jointly on EUPPBench; 16.5% CRPS gain for 2m temperature over raw, beating member-by-member benchmark.

title: Isotonic Distributional Regression
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B (Statistical Methodology)
relevance_note: Isotonic distributional regression - the theory behind EasyUQ and IDR benchmarks.

title: The EUPPBench postprocessing benchmark dataset v1.0
relevance_note: EUPPBench: the standard open benchmark dataset of aligned ECMWF ensemble forecasts and station observations, with a 2m temperature baseline suite.

title: Lead‐time‐continuous statistical postprocessing of ensemble weather forecasts
venue: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society
relevance_note: Lead-time-continuous postprocessing: one model across lead times instead of one model per lead time. Directly reduces the number of fits needed.

title: Easy Uncertainty Quantification (EasyUQ): Generating Predictive Distributions from Single-Valued Model Output
relevance_note: EasyUQ / isotonic distributional regression: turns a SINGLE-VALUED forecast into a calibrated distribution with almost no tuning. The natural baseline for a deterministic AI model.

theme: 7. Multi-station design: semi-local, pooled, unseen locations
title: Similarity-based semi-local estimation of EMOS models
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series C (Applied Statistics)
relevance_note: Semi-local EMOS: augment each station's training data with data from SIMILAR stations, chosen by distance or by clustering on climatology and forecast-error features. The central answer to per-station vs pooled.

theme: 7. Multi-station design: semi-local, pooled, unseen locations
title: Statistical Downscaling of Gridded Wind Speed Data Using Local Topography
relevance_note: Statistical downscaling of gridded wind using local topography descriptors - the terrain-predictor construction pattern.

theme: 7. Multi-station design: semi-local, pooled, unseen locations
title: Clustering-Based Spatial Interpolation of Parametric Postprocessing Models
relevance_note: Clustering-based spatial interpolation of EMOS parameters to locations with NO training data; beats regionally-estimated and interpolated EMOS.

theme: 8. AI forecast models and their postprocessing
title: The Rise of Data-Driven Weather Forecasting: A First Statistical Assessment of Machine Learning–Based Weather Forecasts in an Operational-Like Context
venue: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
relevance_note: First systematic assessment of AI forecast models against IFS - establishes where data-driven models win and where they are smooth/biased.

theme: 8. AI forecast models and their postprocessing
title: Uncertainty quantification for data-driven weather models
relevance_note: Systematic comparison of UQ routes for a deterministic AI model (Pangu): initial-condition ensembles vs statistical/ML post-hoc UQ, over Europe.

theme: 8. AI forecast models and their postprocessing
title: Statistical Postprocessing Yields Accurate Probabilistic Forecasts from Artificial Intelligence Weather Models
venue: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
relevance_note: The most directly relevant paper: an EXISTING operational postprocessing system (IMPROVER) applied unmodified to AIFS at 569 stations. Postprocessing helps AIFS about as much as it helps NWP, and blending AIFS with NWP beats either.

theme: 8. AI forecast models and their postprocessing
title: Probabilistic measures afford fair comparisons of AIWP and NWP model output
relevance_note: Potential CRPS: fair comparison of AI and physical models by subjecting both to the same IDR postprocessing. The correct way to frame 'is AIFS better here'.

theme: 8. AI forecast models and their postprocessing
title: AIFS-CRPS: ensemble forecasting using a model trained with a loss function based on the continuous ranked probability score
relevance_note: AIFS-CRPS: ECMWF's AI ensemble trained on almost-fair CRPS; outperforms the IFS ensemble for most variables at medium range. The user's forecast source.

title: Area-covering postprocessing of ensemble precipitation forecasts using topographical and seasonal conditions
relevance_note: Area-covering EMOS using topographical and seasonal predictors instead of station identity - how to postprocess where there is no station.

title: Seamless multi-model postprocessing for air temperature forecasts in complex topography
relevance_note: Multi-model EMOS blending a convection-permitting LAM with a global ensemble for temperature at Swiss stations; 30% over high-res DMO, 8-12% over single-model EMOS; worst in winter.

title: Convolutional conditional neural processes for local climate downscaling
relevance_note: convCNP downscaling: trained model predicts at ARBITRARY locations including stations with no training data. The 'unseen station' architecture.

title: AIFS -- ECMWF's data-driven forecasting system
relevance_note: AIFS model description (graph transformer encoder-processor-decoder).

title: Graph Neural Networks and Spatial Information Learning for Post-Processing Ensemble Weather Forecasts
relevance_note: GNN postprocessing: stations as graph nodes with attention over neighbours; substantial gain over a strong DRN baseline for 2m temperature over Europe.

title: Gradient-Boosted Mixture Regression Models for Postprocessing Ensemble Weather Forecasts
relevance_note: MIXSAMOS-GB: gradient-boosted MIXTURE regression on standardized anomalies; outperforms state-of-the-art postprocessing for German 2m temperature. Pooled-training + boosting, no deep learning.

title: Uncertainty quantification for data-driven weather models
relevance_note: Preprint version of the Pangu UQ study.

title: Time Series based Ensemble Model Output Statistics for Temperature Forecasts Postprocessing
relevance_note: Preprint version of the time-series EMOS work.

title: An update to ECMWF's machine-learned weather forecast model AIFS
relevance_note: AIFS update: bounding layers for physical consistency, expanded variable set.

title: Earth observation embeddings are effective sub-grid descriptors for probabilistic weather downscaling
relevance_note: Earth-observation foundation-model embeddings as learned sub-grid surface descriptors; +11.5% CRPS for 2m temperature at stations held out in SPACE and time, and works with AI-model input.
